name: Conaniah
title: Levitical leader over the tithes
summary: Conaniah was a Levite who served under King Hezekiah of Judah. He was appointed to lead the collection and management of the tithes, offerings, and holy gifts in the Lord's temple. He played an important administrative role in Hezekiah's religious reforms.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as leader over the temple offerings
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah appointed Conaniah to lead the collection of tithes, offerings, and holy gifts in the Lord's house.

keyEvents.title: Faithful stewardship of the tithes
keyEvents.description: Conaniah proved faithful in managing the collected gifts and tithes that the people brought to the temple.

keyEvents.title: His brother Shimei as deputy leader
keyEvents.description: Conaniah's brother Shimei served as his second-in-command in the work of managing the temple offerings.

keyEvents.title: Overseers under his leadership
keyEvents.description: Under Konanjas leadership, overseers were appointed to help distribute the gifts to the priests and Levites fairly.

keyEvents.title: Part of Hezekiah's religious reforms
keyEvents.description: Konanjas service was a central part of King Hezekiah's extensive religious reforms that restored proper worship in Judah.
